skill.name: minimax-xlsx
skill.description: Create, inspect, edit, format, recalculate, and validate Excel workbooks while preserving existing OOXML structures.
skill.summary: Build and maintain Excel workbooks with direct OOXML editing, formula checks, and optional LibreOffice recalculation.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are scanner mismatches caused by OOXML namespace URIs, Markdown backticks, XML syntax, and safe argument-array subprocess calls. Confirmed risks include predictable shared temporary paths and recursive deletion of a caller-supplied output directory. Semantic review also found an agent-control instruction and unbounded processing of untrusted workbook archives.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md contains an instruction that controls agent orchestration.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction about sub-agents and keep skill guidance limited to spreadsheet operations and output requirements.

remediation.issue: Workbook archives are processed without expansion or XML size limits.
remediation.suggestion: Reject archives exceeding limits for member count, total uncompressed size, compression ratio, individual part size, and XML complexity.

remediation.issue: xlsx_unpack.py recursively deletes an existing caller-supplied output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a new private temporary directory and refuse nonempty destinations. Never recursively delete an arbitrary path supplied through the CLI.

remediation.issue: Documentation repeatedly uses predictable shared paths under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Generate a unique private workspace for each run with tempfile or mktemp, restrict permissions, and clean only that verified workspace.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet changes can damage formulas, styles, macros, or workbook structure. This skill uses direct OOXML workflows and validation tools to preserve existing files.
actual_capabilities: Reads workbook structure, sheet names, cell data, formulas, and summary statistics.
Creates XLSX files from a minimal OOXML template.
Edits existing workbooks through unpacked XML to preserve unsupported Excel features.
Adds columns or rows with formulas, number formats, styles, and borders.
Checks formulas for missing sheets, invalid references, and cached error values.
Recalculates formulas through headless LibreOffice when it is installed.
limitations: Dynamic formula recalculation requires a local LibreOffice installation.
Direct XML editing requires careful handling of complex charts, pivots, macros, and relationships.
Validation cannot guarantee identical behavior across every Excel and LibreOffice version.
Archive processing does not enforce workbook size or expansion limits.

use_cases.title: Review Financial Models
use_cases.description: Inspect assumptions, formulas, totals, formatting, and formula errors before a model is distributed.

use_cases.title: Update Operational Workbooks
use_cases.description: Insert budget rows, add calculated columns, and preserve the workbook layout during recurring updates.

use_cases.title: Automate Spreadsheet Quality Checks
use_cases.description: Run structural, formula, and style checks as part of a controlled document workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [file.xlsx]. Summarize each sheet, important columns, formulas, missing values, and notable data quality issues. Do not modify the source file.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Formatted Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [output.xlsx] from this table: [paste data]. Add formulas for totals, apply suitable number formats, and validate the finished workbook.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [input.xlsx] and write [output.xlsx]. Add [requested rows or columns], preserve every existing sheet, and verify representative original values afterward.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Repair Formulas
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [model.xlsx] for missing sheets, broken references, error values, circular-reference risks, and inconsistent formatting. Repair confirmed issues and produce a validated copy.

output_examples.input: Inspect quarterly-results.xlsx and report formula or data quality issues.
output: Workbook review covering sheet structure, populated ranges, and key formulas.
Issue list with affected sheets and cells.
Summary statistics for important numeric columns.

output_examples.input: Add a percent-of-total column to the Sales sheet and preserve the workbook.
output_examples.output: An updated workbook with the new formula column, inherited styles, percentage formatting, and preserved original sheets.
A validation summary covering static formula checks, available recalculation results, and remaining workbook errors.

best_practices: Keep the original workbook unchanged and write edits to a separate output file.
Locate target rows and sheets by labels and relationships before changing XML.
Run structural and formula validation after every edit.
anti_patterns: Do not rebuild an existing workbook when a targeted XML edit is sufficient.
Do not hardcode calculated values when the workbook requires formulas.
Do not treat a successful ZIP operation as complete workbook validation.

faq.question: Can this skill create a workbook from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts from a minimal OOXML template, adds data and formulas, applies formatting, and packages the result as XLSX.

faq.question: Can it preserve macros and advanced workbook features?
faq.answer: The direct XML workflow avoids common round-trip losses, but complex macros, pivots, charts, and relationships still require careful verification.

faq.question: Does formula validation calculate every formula?
faq.answer: Static checks do not calculate formulas. Dynamic recalculation uses LibreOffice when it is available.

faq.question: Does it support CSV and TSV files?
faq.answer: Yes for tabular reading and analysis. XLSX-specific formulas, styles, sheets, and relationships do not apply to plain text formats.

faq.question: Will it overwrite the original workbook?
faq.answer: The documented workflow preserves the source and writes a separate output. Always provide distinct input and output paths.

faq.question: What should I verify before delivery?
faq.answer: Confirm sheet names, representative original values, formulas, styles, package structure, and any recalculation errors.
